Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFC OF THE FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT OPINION NO 17 S. Ü..&. 03 April 2008 DIRECTOR EVELYN A. TROMPETA DILG Regional Office No. 06 Iloilo City Dear Director Trompeta: This pertains to your Indorsement to this office of the letter of Punong Barangay Cosette Marie M. Belarmino of Barangay Poblacion, Altavas, Aklan, dated 13 December 2007 and the letter of the Members of the Sangguniang Barangay Of the same barangay dated 05 December 2007, with regard to the controversy obtaining in the appointments made bv the newly elected Punong Barangay in favor of the Barangay Treasurer and Barangay secretary. In your referral, you particularly sought clarification on DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2002-150 dated 02 September 2002, entitled: "Guidelines on the Appointment of Barangay Secretaries, Treasurers and Other Appointive Barangay Officials", specifically with respect to section 1, paragraph 2 thereof. TO start with, Section 1, paragraph 2 of said Circular provides that "the Barangay Secretary shall be Of legal age, a qualified voter and an actual resident of the barangay concerned' Your query arose from the following situation, to wit: Punong Barangay Belarmino appointed Mr. Arturo J. Gregorio as Barangay Secretary and Mrs. Adelia Bolivar as Barangay Treasurer. said appointments were then forwarded to the sangguniang Barangay for concurrence in accordance with sections 394 and 395 Of the Local Government code, respectively, which provides that the Barangay Secretary and Barangay Treasurer shall be appointed by the Punong Barangay with the concurrence Of the majority Of all the Sangguniang Barangay Members. on

-2- 05 December 2007, however, the Sangguniang Barangay wrote the DILG Regional Director, informing the latter that thev venementl\/ opposed the appointments issued bv the newly elected Punong Barangay, citing as basis DILG Memorandum Circular NO. 2002-150 dated 02 september 2002 (as aforecited), which requires that the Barangay Treasurer and Barangay Secretary snould be actual residents and are qualified voters of the In tne said letter, the sangguniang Barangay barangay concerned. Members also signified their attestation that the former Barangay Treasurer, Lei D. Quimpo, and Barangay secretary, Elnora C. Losa, be reappointed to the same positions considering that thev have served efficiently. Without dwelling vet on the issue as to whether or not the appointees of Punong Barangay Belarmino are actual residents Of the barangay, allow us in the meantime to discuss the legal requirements in the appointment of Barangay secretary and Barangay Treasurer under the Local Government Code. To start with, mav we point out that the Punong Barangay performs dual functions, namely: ne acts as the local chief executive of tne barangay government per section 389 of the Local Government code, and as Presiding Officer of the Sangguniang Barangay per section 390 of the same Code. It is just proper, therefore, to delineate tne matters to be acted upon by the punong Barangay as local chief executive of the barangay, and the matters to be acted upon by him as presiding Officer of the Sangguniang Barangay. Along this line, in tne case Of Borromeo vs. Mariano (42 Phil. 322), appointment has been defined as "the act of designation by the executive officer to whom that power has been delegated, of the individual who is In this to exercise the functions of a gitæn office" (underlining our S). regard, it is clear, therefore, that the Punong Barangay, in issuing the appointments to the Barangay Treasurer and Barangay Secretary, is doing so in his capacity as local Chief executive of the barangay government and not as presiding Officer of the Sangguniang Barangay. In such capacity as Chief executive, the appointing discretion is exercised solely by him as to who should be selected to perform and exercise the functions of a given office. Pursuant to the provisions of the Local Government code, these appointments, however, are to be submitted to the sangguniang Barangay for concurrence. In the issuance or non-issuance of the concurrence, the Sangguniang Barangay shall be guided solely bv its evaluation of whether the appointees possess the statutorily required qualifications under the Local Government code for the positions (please see secs. 394 and 395 of

-3- the Local Government Code) and none of the disqualifications under the same code and other existing laws. Hence, if the appointees possess all the qualifications and none of the disqualifications, the concurrence shall issue as a matter of course, otherwise, the Sangguniang Barangay shall issue the non-concurrence if the appointees lack any Of the qualifications or possess any Of the disqualifications. It bears to stress that in the 05 December 2007 letter of the Sangguniang Barangay Members, particularly the last paragraph thereof, they signified their intention that the former Barangay Treasurer and Barangay secretary be reappointed considering that thev have served efficiently. we are Of the view that this act of the Sangguniang Barangay directing the reappointment of the former Barangay Treasurer and Barangay secretary is ultra vires or outside the bounds of law as it is not within the scope of their power and authority. It is not amiss to point out that when the appointments were forwarded to the sangguniang Barangay, their only task is to determine the presence or absence Of the qualifications and disqualifications set forth by Sections 39a and 395 of the Local Government code, by the appointees and, accordingly, issue the concurrence or non-concurrence thereto, as the case mav be. It is not wiChin the legal authority of the Sangguniang Barangay to dictate and impose upon the Punong Barangay as to who should be appointed to the positions. If we allow this situation, it would in effect illegally vests unto the sangguniang Barangay the executive power Of appointment which, under the mandate Of Sections 394 and 395, respectively, of the Local Government code, properly belongs to the Punong Barangay as local chief executive. AS local chief executive on whom the power to issue the subject appointments is conferred by law, his action in such capacity is not subject to the dictates and imposition of the Sangguniang Barangay. To do otherwise would be allowing the Sangguniang Barangay to substitute the appointing discretion of the Punong Barangay. In the present situation of poblacion, Altavas, Aklan, the sangguniang Barangay should thus be advised that in issuing the concurrence or non- concurrence, they will simply be guided in determining whether the appointees of the Punong Barangay possess all the qualifications and none of the disqualifications under the Local Government Code. on the issue Of actual residency, mav we note that not onw in the Memorandum Circular of the Department, but also in Sections 394 and 395 of -the Local Government, that the Barangay Treasurer and Barangay secretary are required by law to be actual residents Of the barangay. It is with much regret, however, that you inform the parties concerned that this Department is bereft of anv judicial authority to determine as to

-4- whether or not the appointees of the Punong Barangay are indeed actual residents of Poblacion, Altavas, Aklan. Be that as it may, it is hoped that the Sangguniang Barangay, using its sound discernment and setting aside political motivations and differences, Should Objectively deliberate on the issue Of actual residency based on the preponderance of proof submitted bv the Punong Barangay in justifying his appointments. Short of any ground authorized bv law in not concurring with the appointments, the Punong Barangay or his appointees mav invoke the aid of the court for final judicial findings of the issue. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADER Undersecreta Legal:43/La Punong Barangay Cosette Marie Belarmino Barangay poblacion, Altavas Aklan The Sangguniang Barangay Members Barangay poblacion, Aitavas Aklan
